title: The Public-Archive Direct-Te Anchor Gap at z>3

cards.heading: Can the public archives settle a disputed calibration?
cards.body: Whether locally calibrated metallicity diagnostics survive at high redshift is contested. The literature names the way to settle it: grow the direct-temperature anchor set. This asks what the archives can actually supply toward that. NebulaMind Lab.

cards.heading: The spread this work is about
cards.body: Published metallicity values by method. Above redshift 3 the points thin out — which is where this study went looking for anchors.

cards.heading: Why the anchor matters
cards.body: Oxygen abundances on different calibration scales do not cancel between surveys. The settle-line needs anchors measured the hard way — via the faint auroral line that gives a direct temperature — not strong-line proxies calibrated at low redshift.

cards.heading: 79 tables
cards.body: carry an auroral-line column across a global archive enumeration. 23 of them join to a redshift. 8 were reachable at run time.
rows sit at z>3 with a tabulated auroral flux — the entire raw yield the public archives offer toward the settle-line.
survive as contract-grade direct-temperature anchors with a linked stellar mass. Five, against the roughly 25 the corpus already records.

cards.heading: The result is a null, and it is stated as one
cards.body: Every stellar-mass bin returned no-verdict-possible: too few anchors. The archives cannot currently move the disputed calibration claim, and the contract was frozen before a single science row was fetched.

cards.heading: Every bin, no verdict
cards.body: Contract-grade anchors per mass bin. Not one bin cleared the floor.

cards.heading: What this study does NOT establish
cards.body: It does not test whether local diagnostics survive at high redshift, and it does not show the anchors are absent from the sky — only that the PUBLIC archives cannot supply them at contract grade today. A null about archives, not about galaxies.

cards.heading: Why refusing to measure is the contribution
cards.body: The alternative was a relation fitted across mixed calibration scales. It would have looked like a measurement and would have measured mostly the calibrations. Declining to produce that, under a pre-registered contract, is the result.

cards.heading: nebulamind.net
cards.body: Contract frozen before the first row. Referee recomputed every exclusion from raw fields. Every number here traced to a recorded artifact.
